title: Hall Coefficient Sign Reversal Driven by Orbital-Selective Oxygen-Vacancy Scattering in Nickelate Films
authors: Jian-Jian Miao, Yue Liu, Yue Zhao, Yichen Hua, Changming Yue, Wei-Qiang Chen
abstract: Hall measurements in superconducting bilayer nickelate films show sign reversals that cannot be explained by rigid-band electron doping alone. We combine a DFT+CDMFT-derived correlated multi-orbital quasiparticle model with a $T$-matrix treatment of oxygen-vacancy scattering in a semiclassical Boltzmann transport framework. We find that multiband compensation is insufficient by itself: in-plane vacancies selectively suppress the transport channel dominated by the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital and drive $R_H$ through zero, whereas inner-apical vacancies make $R_H$ more negative. These results identify pocket-resolved and orbital-selective oxygen-vacancy scattering as the microscopic origin of the Hall coefficient sign reversal and provide a framework for oxygen-stoichiometry-dependent transport in nickelate films.
summary: This work theoretically explains the anomalous sign reversal in the Hall coefficient observed in nickelate superconductors. By combining correlated electron theory with detailed scattering calculations, the authors pinpoint that the effect is due to oxygen vacancies selectively disrupting the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital's contribution to transport. This provides a crucial link between material stoichiometry and macroscopic electronic properties.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the microscopic origin of Hall coefficient (R_H) sign reversals observed in superconducting bilayer nickelate films.
main_result: The sign reversal is attributed to orbital-selective scattering caused by oxygen vacancies, specifically showing that in-plane vacancies selectively suppress the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital contribution, driving R_H through zero.
method: A correlated multi-orbital quasiparticle model derived from DFT+CDMFT is combined with a T-matrix treatment of scattering potentials within a semiclassical Boltzmann transport framework.
model_or_system: The system is superconducting bilayer nickelate films containing oxygen vacancies. The theoretical framework involves calculating transport properties using pocket-resolved contributions and modeling the vacancy potential via first-principles DFT calculations.
key_observables: Hall coefficient (R_H), longitudinal conductivity ($\sigma_{aa}$), and orbital-selective Hall contributions ($R_r^H$).
important_parameters: Oxygen-vacancy concentration ($n_{	ext{vac}}$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and the specific type/location of vacancies (in-plane vs. inner-apical).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a dilute-vacancy limit, uses the scalar relaxation-time approximation for scattering rates, and separates rigid-band doping effects from vacancy-induced changes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate quasiparticle Fermi surfaces showing multiple pockets ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma$) and plot R_H vs. $n_{	ext{vac}}$, demonstrating how different vacancy distributions cause the sign reversal through orbital suppression.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes that doping alone fails to explain the sign reversal. It then develops a comprehensive model incorporating orbital selectivity via DFT+CDMFT and T-matrix scattering theory, culminating in quantitative predictions showing the specific role of in-plane vacancies.
why_interesting: While focused on strongly correlated materials, the detailed treatment of transport coefficients (like R_H) using advanced many-body techniques provides a rigorous framework for understanding how local disorder (vacancies) selectively perturbs orbital character and electronic transport channels.
